lines.text: In twenty eleven, underground secret vaults were unlocked in Kerala, India -
revealing over twenty-two billion dollars in solid gold, making it the richest temple in the world.
Beneath the ancient Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram lie six sealed underground chambers.
When a Supreme Court committee opened Vault A,
they were blinded by mountains of gold coins from the Roman Empire and Napoleonic era,
hundreds of diamond-encrusted crowns, and an eighteen-foot pure gold necklace!
The discovered treasure was valued at over one lakh eighty thousand crore rupees.
But the deepest chamber, Vault B, remains completely unopened.
Its entrance is guarded by a massive iron door carved with giant king cobras without any locks or latches.
Ancient temple legends warn that Vault B is locked by a mystical sound binding called Naga Bandham,
and forcing it open without sacred secret chants will trigger catastrophic disasters across the ocean!
Subscribe to discover more incredible Indian mysteries, and hit like if you think Vault B should stay sealed!
